article.title: Why Historical Data Can Encode Yesterday’s Business Rules
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Historical data is often treated as a record of customer behavior, but it is also a record of past business decisions. Who received an offer, whose application was approved, which transactions were reviewed, and which customers remained eligible were shaped by policies that existed at the time. A model trained on those outcomes can therefore learn yesterday’s operating rules as well as underlying behavior. Consider a credit model trained only on approved applicants. Outcomes for rejected applicants are not observed, so the training sample reflects the previous approval policy. A marketing model may learn that certain customers rarely convert simply because old campaigns rarely contacted them. A fraud dataset may contain more confirmed fraud among transactions that prior rules sent to investigators because unreviewed cases were less likely to receive labels. These are forms of selective labels and policy feedback. The problem becomes visible when the organization changes strategy. A new model may be asked to score a broader population than the one represented in historical labels. Relationships learned under the old policy may not transport cleanly. Analysts should document how labels were created, who could enter the training population, and what previous decisions affected observation. Policy variables can sometimes be useful features, but including them does not automatically remove selection bias. In some settings, randomized exploration or carefully designed holdout policies can collect information outside the historical decision boundary. Causal or missing-data methods may also help, but their assumptions need scrutiny. Temporal validation is especially important when policies changed over time. A performance drop after deployment may reflect a change in decision rules rather than a mysterious failure of machine learning. Governance should therefore version not only models and datasets but also major eligibility, approval, campaign, and labeling rules. Historical data is never completely neutral. It was produced by a system of people, policies, incentives, and previous models. Understanding that system helps teams distinguish stable behavioral signal from artifacts of yesterday’s decisions. Analysts should define the population, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed pattern from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文重點在於把 model metric 或 KPI 放回實際 decision context。數字變大不一定更好；極端群體可能自然回歸平均；ranking 與 probability calibration 是不同能力；歷史資料也會承載舊政策；而 campaign 真正關心的常常是 intervention 所創造的增量效果。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：model metricやKPIはdecision contextの中で解釈する必要がある。数値が大きいこと自体が良いとは限らず、極端群は平均へ回帰し、rankingとprobability calibrationは別の性能である。historical dataには旧policyも刻まれ、campaignではinterventionによる増分効果が重要になる。
